what_happened: The person running Athena used a hand-written approve-then-drain script. It approved a job that changed Athena's own code, then started the next queue batch without rebuilding. The batch began on the old build. Athena's new stale-build check flagged it. The person stopped the batch and rebuilt before any work ran. No job was involved. The script left out the rebuild step that their other scripts run after a landing.
cause: Rebuilding after a landing that changes Athena's own code is a manual step that each hand-written script must remember. Athena has no single command that approves, rebuilds if needed and then drains. It also does not rebuild or refuse to start a drain when the installed binary is older than the landed code. The stale-build check only warns after the batch has started, so safety depends on every script copying the rebuild step.
prevention: Make drain, and any command that starts a batch, compare the installed binary's build with the repo head at start. If the binary is older, drain should refuse to dispatch anything and print the rebuild command, or rebuild and re-exec itself. Add one tracked command that approves, rebuilds when Athena's code changed, and then starts the drain. Hand scripts then no longer carry the rebuild step. The existing stale-build check should become a blocking pre-dispatch gate rather than a flag raised after start.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain refuse to dispatch work when the installed Athena binary is older than the code at the repository head. Today the stale-build check only flags it after a batch has started. Outcome: when drain starts, or between items after a landing that changed Athena's own code or config schema, it compares the installed build with the head. If they differ, it dispatches nothing, records a clear message naming the rebuild step, and exits with a distinct status. Add one tracked command that approves a job, rebuilds if the landing changed Athena's code, and then starts the drain, so hand scripts need no rebuild step of their own. Acceptance: a test with a stale binary shows drain dispatches no item and prints the rebuild instruction. A test with a current binary shows drain proceeds as before. A test shows the combined command rebuilds only when the landing changed Athena's code.
